recommendedTextbook.title: Basic Technology for Junior Secondary Schools 1
recommendedTextbook.author: P.B. Nwachukwu, O.A. Adebayo, C.O. Ibe

topics.topic: Understanding Technology: Meaning, Technology in Nigeria & Career Paths
subtopics: Definition of technology as applied science to solve human problems
Indigenous technology in Nigeria (blacksmithing, cloth weaving, pottery, canoe carving)
Modern STEM careers: civil, electrical, mechanical, software engineering, and architecture
objectives: Define technology and differentiate science (knowing) from technology (doing)
Appraise indigenous Nigerian technological inventions in traditional industries
State four modern engineering career options for Nigerian secondary students

topics.topic: Workshop Safety Rules, First Aid and Protective Equipment (PPE)
subtopics: Causes of workshop accidents (carelessness, horseplay, faulty tools, wet floors)
Workshop safety rules and Personal Protective Equipment (safety goggles, boots, aprons, gloves)
First aid box contents and treatment of simple cuts, burns, and fainting spells
objectives: List 10 statutory safety rules governing secondary school technical workshops
Demonstrate immediate first aid protocols for a minor workshop laceration or thermal burn

topics.topic: Safety Signs and Color Codes: Prohibition, Warning & Mandatory
subtopics: Red circular signs: Prohibition (e.g., No Smoking, No Naked Flames)
Yellow triangular signs: Caution and Hazard Warning (e.g., Flammable, High Voltage)
Blue circular signs: Mandatory instructions (e.g., Wear Ear Protection, Wear Helmet)
Green rectangular signs: Safety equipment and Emergency Exits
objectives: Interpret industrial safety color codes and geometric symbols
Draw and color three standard workshop safety caution signs

topics.topic: Identification of Materials I: Hardwoods vs Softwoods in Nigeria
subtopics: Classification of trees: deciduous hardwoods (broad leaves, fruit-bearing) vs coniferous softwoods (needle-like leaves)
Common Nigerian commercial hardwoods: Iroko, Mahogany, Obeche, Teak, Afara
Physical properties and structural uses of timber in roofing and furniture
objectives: Differentiate hardwoods from softwoods based on leaf morphology and seed structure
Identify wood samples collected from local sawmills in timber-producing states

topics.topic: Identification of Materials II: Ferrous vs Non-Ferrous Metals
subtopics: Definition of metals and extraction from mineral ores
Ferrous metals containing iron: cast iron, wrought iron, mild steel, high-carbon steel
Non-ferrous metals containing no iron: aluminum, copper, zinc, lead, brass, bronze
objectives: Distinguish ferrous from non-ferrous metals using bar magnets and visual luster
State applications of copper (electrical cables) and aluminum (roofing sheets, aircraft)

topics.topic: Identification of Materials III: Ceramics, Plastics and Rubber
subtopics: Ceramics: clay, cement, glass, tiles, bricks, and their heat-resistant properties
Plastics: thermoplastics (can be remolded by heating) vs thermosetting plastics
Natural rubber (latex from rubber trees) vs synthetic rubber (petrochemical origin)
objectives: Classify household plastic products into thermoplastics (polyethene) and thermosetting (Bakelite plugs)
Explain vulcanization of natural rubber for vehicle tires

subtopics: Diagnostic evaluation on safety rules, signs, wood, metals, plastics, and ceramics
Workshop safety drill assessment
objectives: Assess pupil mastery of basic technology foundational modules

topics.topic: Technical Drawing Instruments and Proper Board Setup
subtopics: Drawing instruments: drawing board, T-Square, 30°/60° and 45° set-squares, metric ruler, French curves
Fastening drawing paper onto board with masking tape: aligning with working edge of T-Square
Ruling standard 10mm border margins and constructing the title block
objectives: Align drawing paper parallel to the working edge of the T-Square without wrinkles
Rule clean 10mm border lines and complete a standard 3-row title block

topics.topic: Technical Lettering and Line Types in Drafting
subtopics: Single-stroke upright capital lettering between 3mm and 5mm guidelines
Alphabet of lines: thick continuous (visible outlines), thin continuous (dimension/projection lines)
Thin dashed lines (hidden details), thin long/short dash (center lines)
objectives: Execute neat, uniform engineering lettering without flourishes
Draw five statutory drafting line types with correct pencil weights (2H for construction, HB for outlines)

topics.topic: Woodwork Hand Tools: Measuring, Marking Out and Sawing
subtopics: Measuring tools: steel tape rule, steel rule, try square (checking 90° squareness)
Marking out tools: scriber, marking gauge, mortise gauge, center punch
Sawing hand tools: rip saw, crosscut saw, tenon saw, coping saw
objectives: Check squareness of a wooden block using a try square
Select the correct saw for cutting along wood grain (rip saw) vs across grain (crosscut saw)

topics.topic: Bench Work & Tool Maintenance: Cleaning, Oiling and Storage
subtopics: Care and maintenance of woodworking tools: cleaning sawdust, applying light machine oil to prevent rust
Proper tool storage in tool racks and shadow boards
Sharpening plane irons and wood chisels on an oilstone
objectives: Sharpen a chisel blade on an oilstone maintaining the correct 25° grinding angle
State reasons for storing cutting hand tools separately to prevent dulling

topics.topic: Comprehensive Termly Revision & Practical Drafting Workshop
subtopics: Review of materials, safety, drawing board practice, and hand tools
Timed practical engineering drafting test
objectives: Complete a standardized JSS 1 Basic Technology drafting dossier

subtopics: Terminal practical and theory examination
objectives: Complete JSS 1 Basic Technology certification
